title: Joint H1 injectivity of residue-field product slices
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ and $g:Y\to S$ be proper morphisms of schemes [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-pc-scheme], with sections $\sigma:S\to X$ and $\tau:S\to Y$ [def-pc-section]. Suppose their canonical structure-pushforward units are isomorphisms after every base change [def-pc-base-change, lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction]. For $s\in S$ put $p:X\times_S Y\to S$ [def-pc-fibre-product] and let $i_X=(1,\tau f):X\to X\times_S Y$ and $i_Y=(\sigma g,1):Y\to X\times_S Y$. Then the base changes of these maps along $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to S$ induce an injective map $H^1((X\times_S Y)_s,\mathcal O)\to H^1(X_s,\mathcal O)\times H^1(Y_s,\mathcal O)$ [def-sc-structure-sheaf-cohomology-pullback, def-weil-residue-field].

proof.text: Evaluate the tensor-pullback adjunction unit on the structure sheaf after base change to Spec κ(s). By tensorPullbackObjUnitToUnit_isIso, the structure-sheaf map is the composite of this unit with pushforward of an isomorphism. Evaluation at any open U makes the structure-sheaf ring map on U an isomorphism; specialize this general comparison to the top open to make appTop an isomorphism. Composing with ΓSpecIso proves bijectivity of the canonical scalar maps. Base change the sections to rational points using pullback.lift; properness is stable under base change. Apply picard_h1_product_injective over κ(s).

Construct the product base-change isomorphism explicitly in both directions by pullback.lift and verify its inverse identities by pullback.hom_ext. Verify by the same universal property that the base-changed slices followed by this isomorphism are the rational-point slices. Transport two cohomology classes by pullback along the inverse isomorphism. Functoriality identifies their slice images, so field-product injectivity makes their transported classes equal. Pullback along the forward isomorphism and the identity law recover equality of the original classes.

proof_origin.description: The original two-step route formalized with explicit pullback pasting, top-open evaluation of the adjunction unit, and functorial cohomology transport. Repair: generalize the private structure-sheaf comparison to arbitrary opens, rather than duplicating the private top-open theorem in PicardLocusClosedValuativeFactorization.
